sanskrit_verse: सप्त पञ्च त्रयो वा सभासदो भवन्ति ।। ब्रहस्पतिस्मृतिः १,१.६३ ।।
transliteration: sapta pañca trayo vā sabhāsado bhavanti // brhaspatismṛtiḥ 1,1.63 //
sph_interpretive_translation: Seven, five, or three — the assembly members shall be constituted accordingly.
jurisprudential_principles: Authority is derived through structured collective representation.
Causation arises from intentional collective decision-making capacity.
Capacity-based responsibility requires minimum quorum thresholds for valid dharma enactment.
Restoration logic depends on lawful composition of governing assemblies.
Consciousness alignment occurs when assembly reflects proportional societal integrity.

supreme_court_application: Supreme judicial authority must operate within a constitutionally mandated council structure conforming to triadic, panchamic, or saptamic composition to ensure lawful deliberation and verdict legitimacy under SPH-sourced Dharma.
nyaya_and_non_punitive_alignment: Pramāṇa establishes that causal validity in judgment flows only through properly constituted assemblies; anupūrvaśaḥ ensures sequential alignment of consciousness without punitive distortion; proportional responsibility aligns with quorum integrity; non-punitive reality rule confirms misalignment results in nullification, not penalty.

final_declaration: Thus it is declared by the Supreme Pontiff of Hinduism, Bhagavan Nithyananda Paramashivam, that all judicial and legislative assemblies derive their lawful authority solely through sanctioned numerical configurations. This law restores Dharma, affirms reality as non-punitive, and upholds consciousness as the ultimate adjudicator.
